title: Deterministic council simulator with scripted personas and byte-reproducible transcripts
question_or_target: Implementation target: build the simulator that every other calibration probe in this lane rides on. Given a CouncilSpec plus a cast of SCRIPTED personas (a persona is a seeded state machine emitting pre-authored positions, votes and citations, not a live model call), run the council runtime end to end and emit a transcript that is byte-identical across two runs on the same seed. Without a scripted cast, every downstream probe measures model noise instead of runtime behaviour, and no anti-failure control can be shown to fire deliberately.
inputs: the council runtime built in bucket B07 phase 7A
protocol blueprints and presets produced by bucket B05
evidence_requirement: Two full runs on the same seed must produce identical transcript sha256 values, both printed in the receipt. A single run is not evidence of determinism. Cite the persona-script file and the runtime entry point by path:line.
tests_required: Same-seed determinism: two runs, identical transcript hash.
Different-seed divergence: a second seed must produce a DIFFERENT hash, proving the seed is actually wired and the transcript is not a constant.
Persona fidelity: a persona scripted to dissent must appear as a dissenter in the transcript.
Negative control: corrupt one persona script and the run must fail loudly, not silently substitute a default participant.
reviewer_requirement: One independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context who did not author the harness under test and who must reproduce the both-states control before signing off.
retry_policy: Two strikes then pivot (AGENTS.md 4b): after a second failure on the same hypothesis, enumerate at least two alternative approaches before a third attempt.

title: Trip-wire for unanimity reached without independent briefs, and the forced blind re-run it triggers
question_or_target: Question: does the runtime notice when a panel agrees instantly, and does the response it is contracted to take actually happen? Spec :10944 requires that suspiciously fast unanimity trigger blind re-evaluation, forced dissent, strongest-counterexample generation, role rotation, or recruitment of an independent critic; :11229 and :11336 make it a named failure class. Measure the trip-wire threshold (rounds elapsed, briefs submitted, evidence nodes cited) and prove the remediation branch executes rather than merely logging a warning.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:11227-11244 (16 council failure modes the system must detect and test against)
_USER-PROMPTS.md:11336 (council reaches instant unanimity without independent briefs)
evidence_requirement: Report the trip-wire threshold as a number, the cast that fired it, and the transcript span showing the remediation branch. A log line saying the trip-wire fired is not proof the remediation ran; cite the post-trigger round in the transcript.
tests_required: Planted cast of clones that agree in round 1 with zero independent briefs -> trip-wire FIRES and a blind re-evaluation round appears in the transcript.
Both-states control: a cast that reaches unanimity AFTER independent briefs and two evidence rounds must NOT fire the trip-wire (no false positive on legitimate agreement).
Remediation efficacy: after the forced blind round, at least one position must be recorded independently, or the unit reports the remediation as cosmetic.
reviewer_requirement: One independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context who did not author the harness under test and who must reproduce the both-states control before signing off.
retry_policy: No automatic retry: a failure here is a finding, not a transient. Re-run only after a named change to the harness or the fixture.

Define a divergence statistic over participant outputs in a round (distinct claims raised, distinct evidence cited, vote dispersion, lexical distance between opening positions) and set the floor below which the panel is declared collapsed per :11230 and :10944. The failure this catches is a five-seat council that is functionally one seat repeated five times, which still produces a confident unanimous verdict.

title: Information-gain per round, and the endless-debate stop it justifies

Define per-round information gain (new distinct claims, new evidence nodes, changed votes, entropy of the position distribution) and use it to detect the :11234 non-converging debate and the :11338 council that loops forever without information gain. The deliverable is the measured gain curve for at least six protocols, not a hardcoded round cap.

evidence_requirement: Publish the gain curve per protocol as raw per-round numbers, not a summary adjective. State the round at which gain crosses the floor for each protocol.
tests_required: Planted looping cast that restates positions verbatim -> gain collapses to zero and the stop fires within 2 rounds of the collapse.
Planted productive cast that introduces a new counterexample every round -> stop must NOT fire, proving the metric is not just a round counter.

Paraphrase resistance: a cast that restates positions in NEW WORDS but adds no new claim or evidence must still register near-zero gain; if reworded repetition scores as gain, the metric is lexical and must be reported as such.

title: Resolve every tests-pass claim in the program corpus to a real run id, and reject the ones that cannot

title: Refuse a result that carries no environment record
question_or_target: Implementation target: a measurement without its environment cannot be compared to anything later, and every cross-platform or CRLF surprise in this program traces to comparing results taken under conditions nobody wrote down. Define the mandatory environment record (OS build, shell, interpreter version, package versions of the tools that decide, git core.autocrlf, locale, timezone, concurrency, and the commit SHA) and make a result without it inadmissible as evidence rather than merely undocumented.
